reasons.A1: Select one conditional research hypothesis. Changing an existing evaluator's algorithm and jointly deriving initialization, event updates and outputs creates a concrete question about explaining and consistently editing coupled private rules. This is stronger than local expression expansion as a research target, but neither missing source structure nor larger maintained state establishes resistance. The public-history sidecar and clean transition extractor may still defeat it cheaply.
reasons.A2: Do not select. A direct globally resynthesized circuit is technically distinct, but no concrete existing noncryptographic kernel and partial edit has survived the known-operation, clean-netlist and legitimate-cost challenges. A second slot would currently fund an unsupported mechanism rather than a discriminating experiment.
reasons.A3: Do not select as an independent architecture. Future-behavior minimization may assist clean extraction, and history count is not difficulty. Proven residualization can support A1 without becoming a second protection claim or concealing its own easy extraction route.

requiredConditions: This ballot selects research only. It neither approves a new production implementation nor changes the current regional NO-GO decision or the earlier functional-recovery stopping rules.

Freeze three existing evaluator roots, their public event/observation contracts, and partial edit/explanation tickets before selecting favorable algorithm realizations. Report unsupported roots and inapplicable algorithm families as failures or limits; do not replace them silently with synthetic kernels.

Preserve every accepted source behavior, including initialization/reset, deletion semantics, duplicate multiplicities, order, identities, exceptions and all future observations. Bounds must follow from source semantics. Delete-by-key and escaping-record contracts may require retaining source records; do not modify the API or falsely claim that required state disappeared.

Give ordinary and transformed implementations identical ticket information, public schema, examples, queries and attack resources. Audit whether a ticket plus public inputs already specifies a complete replacement; do not conceal that information or require a preferred decoding method.

Allow full artifact and compiler access, known seeds, instrumentation, patching, arbitrary added state, public-history logging, reset/replay, omitted or synthesized events, black-box learning, sidecar evaluators and global replacement. No inaccessible secret, restricted event history or no-reset assumption may be introduced.

Require measured improvement in both predictive comprehension and valid partial edits on held-out targets and histories. Explanations must predict relevant effects and invariants; edits must preserve unspecified unchanged behavior. Original identifiers, exact source attribution and discarded irrelevant details do not count as success criteria.

Measure functional replacement separately and disclose any cheap clone even if explanation or edit tasks remain harder. Cosmetic AST/SSA rewriting is not recovery; a clean usable model that removes realization machinery does count. Never promote an edit-only result into anti-cloning or cryptographic security.

Record wall time, CPU, memory, model tokens, analyst effort, setup and transfer separately; unknown effort stays unknown. Use the cheapest successful attack lane and the same resource envelope on both sides. Record legitimate cold start, runtime, size, peak memory, build cost and admission rate.

Stop the candidate if a reusable sidecar, replay strategy, rule learner or clean extractor solves the relevant tasks at comparable cost, or if correctness, admission or legitimate resource limits fail. Do not spend a second slot merely to fill the quota.
cheapestDefeat: Log public initialization and event histories, retain tuples or all necessary derived state in a sidecar, and implement the ticket's change in a clean ordinary evaluator while obtaining unchanged coupled behavior by replay, synthetic events, black-box learning or artifact extraction. If that works cheaply, removing base tuples or obscuring update invariants provides no advantage. Independently test a clean transition extractor for functional replacement.
firstExperiment: Before implementing the architecture, audit three existing deterministic evaluator roots and their unchanged APIs, then freeze partial edit and predictive explanation tickets with identical information for ordinary and transformed versions. Attempt the public-history sidecar and replay attacks against those tickets first. For surviving eligible roots, produce three genuinely applicable algorithm families under fixed exactness and resource limits; compare clean transition extraction, domain reconstruction, edits and explanations from reset on held-out deletion, duplicate, boundary and untouched-behavior histories. Report admission failures and cheap clones explicitly. Advance only if both comprehension and edit results survive the cheapest admissible attack and legitimate-cost gates.
